public.summary: Four runners, four legs, three rules. Find a running order that works.
public.statement: Four friends — Ana, Ben, Cy, and Dee — are running a four-leg charity relay. Each person runs exactly one leg. Choose a running order for legs 1 to 4 that follows every rule. There may be more than one valid order; any order that follows all the rules is accepted.
facts: Leg 1 starts at the park gate and leg 4 finishes at the stadium.
Cy is recovering from a sprained ankle and wants a middle leg on flat ground.

constraints.text: Each runner runs exactly one leg.
Cy runs neither the first nor the last leg.
Ana runs an earlier leg than Ben.
Dee's leg is not directly before or directly after Cy's leg.

public.explanation_prompt: Where did you start? Did you notice whether more than one order works?

provenance.author: Reasoning Lab project team
provenance.contamination_note: Original task with two valid answers; ordering puzzles of this shape are common online.

anchors.alternatives: Stating that a second valid order exists counts as an explicit alternative.

reviewed_explanation.text: Cy must run leg 2 or leg 3. If Cy runs leg 2, Dee cannot run legs 1 or 3, so Dee runs leg 4; Ana and Ben fill legs 1 and 3 with Ana first: Ana, Cy, Ben, Dee. If Cy runs leg 3, Dee cannot run legs 2 or 4, so Dee runs leg 1; Ana and Ben fill legs 2 and 4: Dee, Ana, Cy, Ben. Both orders follow every rule.
reviewed_explanation.accepted_summary: Two valid orders: Ana–Cy–Ben–Dee or Dee–Ana–Cy–Ben.

review.notes: Two solutions by design, to test that valid alternative answers are accepted.
